title: Investigate scheduler-throttle interaction causing KV-cache deadlocks and long-context tail regressions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Multiple customers (notably AcmeHealth and NordicRetail) reported sudden latency regressions on mixed-length workloads after recent throttle/quotas fix. Rootly ticket and support transcripts point to long-context tail spikes caused by scheduler admission collapse and KV-cache eviction churn under tenant-level throttling events. This ticket centralizes investigation and coordinates a production bugfix across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
impact_summary: High impact: production P0 for two enterprise customers (SLA violations observed). Symptoms include sustained 95th/99th percentile token latency increases (x2-4) during microburst patterns, elevated error rates for streaming responses, and stalled canaries on Dedicated pools. Affects all deployment modes when mixed short/long sequences and tenant throttles coincide.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use synthetic traffic generator with 80% short requests (16-64 tokens) and 20% long requests (>=2048 tokens) targeting a single tenant.
2) Enable per-tenant throttle: admission limit reduced to 60% of baseline for 30s to simulate quota enforcement.
3) Observe scheduler admission reservoir shrink and preferential queuing of long-context requests; KV-cache eviction spikes when long requests flush large caches.
4) Measure tail latency on short requests — 95th/99th increases and occasional stall >10s reproduces within 60s in our staging clusters.
root_cause_hypothesis: A race between the admission controller that enforces tenant throttles and the batching scheduler's fairness heuristics causes the admission reservoir to be rebalanced aggressively toward in-flight long requests. Long requests hold large KV cache segments; when admission drops, background eviction and KV handoffs create head-of-line blocking and a feedback loop that suppresses small-request throughput. Additionally, the throttle-induced backpressure reduces the scheduler's preemption opportunities, preventing timely dequeue of long requests.
proposed_fixes: Short-term mitigation: deploy an emergency lane for latency-sensitive short requests (configurable per-tenant) to bypass admission shrinkage until reservoir stabilizes.
Medium-term fix: add hysteresis to admission reservoir resizing so reservoir reductions occur gradually and avoid starving short-request flows during transient throttles.
KV-cache guard: pin active KV contexts for in-progress short requests for a short grace period to prevent eviction churn when a tenant's effective admission is lowered.
Scheduler enhancement: implement opportunistic preemption hook that can preempt long-context batches when short-request backlog exceeds a threshold and preemption budget is available.

Operational: create a deterministic canary that replays mixed-length traffic at release gates and add specific Grafana alerts for 'kv_eviction_rate' and 'admission_reservoir_delta' correlated to tenant throttles.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Repro test in staging with synthetic mixed workload shows <10% regression in 99th latency for short requests when tenant throttle toggles compared to baseline.
2) Deployed hotfix to Hosted with emergency lane and hysteresis reduces incidents for affected customers to zero for 72 hours under load tests.
3) KV eviction metrics no longer spike in lockstep with admission reservoir drops in test clusters.
4) PR has unit and integration tests exercising preemption and reservoir hysteresis logic.
5) Runbook updated and shared with Customer Success for immediate mitigation steps.
